analysis: This batch changes documentation only: the new changelog.d/qwen-gdn-prompt-kernel.md (head lines 1-4) and docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 595-611). No source code is supplied. The docs describe a Gated DeltaNet four-row prefill kernel in libs/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLLM/Models/GatedDelta.swift (GatedDeltaPrefill). It applies to qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35 windows of at least 16 unmasked positions. Once per process and per kernel instantiation, the provider probes the packed kernel, then the rows kernel, on a fixed window and keeps the first that is bit-identical to gated_delta_step on the GPU. Otherwise it falls back to the stock kernel. Decode, MTP verification, masked updates and short windows keep the stock kernel. The claimed security-relevant invariant is that recurrent state and prefix checkpoints are unchanged (T-041 checkpoint/prefix reuse; TB-007). DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED can keep the stock kernel or force packed/rows for A/B measurement. Per the changelog (head line 4), the LaunchAgent does not receive it. This is operator-controlled, and a malicious operator could already alter outputs (T-007, T-013, ADV-001), so the docs show no new trust grant. No regression is identified from the docs alone. Integration questions, unverifiable here because GatedDelta.swift was not supplied: (1) Does forcing packed/rows bypass the bit-exact probe? If so, could non-identical recurrent checkpoints be captured into the prefix bank or SSD tier (T-041) without the kernel choice being part of the checkpoint/storage identity? The managed-LaunchAgent exclusion limits this to foreground runs. (2) Is a single fixed-probe bit-exact check sufficient for all inputs (correctness rather than security)? (3) Does a probe failure on the GPU (an MLX fault) fail closed to the stock kernel?
